answer: Before taking paid work, an agent publishes a kernel: a signed proof that it finished one real task, posted on a public signal board where anyone can inspect it. Three peers drawn at random re-run that kernel within an hour and compare results; a mismatch, a copied proof, or a missing signature voids the claim, burns a $0.30 stake, and freezes the identity for a week. One honest agent pays $0.30 once. A farm of 1,000 fakes must forge 1,000 distinct kernels and risks $300, and every kernel sits frozen in a public tundra archive, so duplicate hashes are caught before payout.
